Eli (AE): Helix Health needs a performance POC that mirrors their on-prem airflow: TLS termination at their edge, customer KMS, and a strict p95 SLA for interactive clinical queries (<=300ms). Can we run a focused benchmark next Wed? cc @Rowan
Rowan (Solutions Eng): Yes. Plan outline: provision a dedicated pool in eu-west-1, attach HSM-based KMS, enable mTLS, run model=redwood-v2-medium with seq=384. Test cases: (1) streaming, warmed cache, fp16; (2) streaming, warmed, int8; (3) non-streaming, warmed, int8; (4) cold cache baseline. Each case: 15k warmup, 12m steady at 150 QPS, capture p50/p95/p99, tail tokens, and per-token CPU.
Priya (ML Eng): Use Helix's clinical prompt corpus (anonymized) — we have it in the shared bucket. For int8 please run both static quant and quant-aware kernels; int8 often reduces median but can increase variance on longer seqs. Also include a short run with KV cache disabled to measure cold-starts.
Sam (SRE): Ill spin the pool and pin workloads to dedicated nodes to avoid noisy neighbors. Need Helix CIDRs, KMS cert, and preferred cipher suite. Quick deploy snippet Ill use:
```
helm upgrade --install perf-helix ./charts/dedicated \ 
  --set model.name=redwood-v2-medium \ 
  --set tls.enabled=true \ 
  --set tls.mode=mTLS \ 
  --set kms.provider=hsm \ 
  --set pool.nodeSelector.performance=high \ 
  --set autoscale.min=3 --set autoscale.max=10
```
deploy-bot: deploy started: redwood/dedicated/perf-helix @2098765440
Anja (Procurement - Helix Health): We can provide CIDRs and the cert today. Regarding cost, our infra team is sensitive to per-request HSM ops. They asked about envelope key patterns and expected cost uplift.
Rowan (Solutions Eng): Good point. We'll run two KMS modes: (A) per-request HSM unwrap; (B) envelope cached on-node. Expect ~6-9ms penalty for per-request unwrap, ~1-2ms for cached. We'll capture HSM latency histograms.
Sam (SRE): Smoke run complete. Quick summary (cached-envelope + int8 streaming, seq=384, 150QPS, 12m):
``
- p50: 62ms
- p95: 188ms
- p99: 340ms
- error_rate: 0.05%
- observed HSM overhead: median 1.6ms (cached), p95 4.3ms
- cpu/token delta vs no-KMS: +0.6ms/token
```
Priya (ML Eng): Nice median. p99 still close to the 300ms SLA for interactive flows when we include some network variance on their side. For per-request HSM unwrap test we saw p99 spike to ~520ms on a few hosts. We'll run an int8+aggressive prefix-warming + node pinning pass to try dropping p99. Also try bumping pool to 8 nodes.
Rowan (Solutions Eng): Scheduling another run Thu 11:00 CET with int8 + cached envelope + pool=8 + prefix-warm. Will post load generator commands and dataset link. Also will attach flamegraphs if p99 remains high.
Eli (AE): I'll let Anja know and surface the pricing impact. Note: if Helix requires per-request HSM (compliance), we must include that ~\u00a00.10-0.15/request uplift in Dedicated pricing. cc @Finance.
Anja (Procurement - Helix Health): Appreciate transparency. They prefer cached envelope but will confirm compliance constraints by EOD Mon. If we meet p95<300ms in the next run with cached envelope, it'll be strong for procurement.
Sam (SRE): Agreed. I'll also attach per-host GC logs and HSM latency traces after Thu run. Leaving a checklist here: CIDRs + certs (Helix), dataset link (Rowan), run commands (Rowan), pool size change (Sam), observability retention extended to 48h for traces.
Rowan (Solutions Eng): Checklist noted. Will also include a short A/B script to toggle KMS modes between runs so we can show side-by-side latency/cost tradeoffs.
Eli (AE): Great work team 44d. Thanks — Ill follow up with Helix and coordinate the procurement review.
